heading: Liji 14 · Da Zhuan 大傳 · The Great Treatise · Da Zhuan 15 … Da Zhuan 19

items.text: Revere the Head of your branch because he continues the line from the High Ancestor.
items.quote: They honoured the Ancestor, and therefore they reverenced the Head. The reverence showed the significance of that honour.

items.text: Honor your ancestors by revering their tablets and offering sacrifices in the ancestral temple.
items.quote: From the affection for parents came the honouring of ancestors; from the honouring of the ancestor came the respect and attention shown to the Heads.
items.conflict: Worship God alone; honor ancestors by remembering them, not by sacrificial offerings.

items.text: Appoint a full brother, if an officer or great officer, to be the Honoured Head for your half-brothers.
items.quote: for all his half-brothers who were officers and Great officers appoint a full brother, also an officer or a Great officer, to be the Honoured Head.

items.text: Wear mourning for a kinsman according to the degree of kinship; cease mourning when kinship is no longer counted.
items.quote: When the kinship was no longer counted, there was no further wearing of mourning. The kinship was the bond of connexion.
items.conflict: The dead are not to be worshiped; mourning expresses love and loss but not veneration.

heading: Liji 14 · Da Zhuan 大傳 · The Great Treatise · Da Zhuan 1 … Da Zhuan 14

items.text: Offer the ancestral sacrifice to your grandfather; you are the Honoured Head through whom the line continues.
items.quote: did not sacrifice to his grandfather--to show there was the Honoured Head (who should do so)

items.text: If you are not the eldest son, do not offer the ancestral sacrifice to your grandfather; that belongs to the Honoured Head.
items.quote: Any son but the eldest... did not sacrifice to his grandfather

items.text: Wear mourning for kinsmen according to the prescribed degrees: for four generations reduced to three months; after the sixth generation the bond ends.
items.quote: For parties four generations removed... the mourning was reduced to that worn for three months... After the sixth generation the bond of kinship was held to be at an end.

items.text: If you are not the continuator of your grandfather, do not wear the three-year mourning for your eldest son; he is not the continuator of your line.
items.quote: Nor could he wear mourning for his eldest son for three years, because he was not the continuator of his grandfather.

items.text: Do not marry anyone who shares your original surname, no matter how many generations have passed.
items.quote: there could be no intermarriage, even after a hundred generations
items.conflict: Scripture permits marriage beyond close kin; only specific near relations are forbidden (Leviticus 18).

items.text: Assemble and feast all the members of your kindred, as the way of the head of the clan.
items.quote: It was the way for the ruler to assemble and feast all the members of his kindred.

items.text: Respect the aged, for no change can be made in the respect due to them.
items.quote: the respect due to the aged

items.text: Show affection to your kinsman; no change may be made in what concerns affection for kin.
Honor those who are honourable; this is unchangeable.
items.quote: the honour paid to the honourable

items.text: Use the correct relational titles for family members, for the name is of great importance in regulating the family.
items.quote: The name or appellation is of the greatest importance in the regulation of the family.
